**Top 5 most‑populous cities (city‑proper) – 2023 estimates** | Rank | City (Country) | City‑proper population* | Source | |------|----------------|------------------------|--------| | 1 | **Tokyo, Japan** | ≈ 37.4 million | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities | | 2 | **Delhi, India** | ≈ 31.2 million | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities | | 3 | **Shanghai, China** | ≈ 27.1 million | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities | | 4 | **São Paulo, Brazil** | ≈ 22.0 million | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities | | 5 | **Mexico City, Mexico** | ≈ 21.8 million | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities | \*“City‑proper” = population within the official administrative boundaries of the municipality (as presented in the *city‑proper* table on the Wikipedia “List of largest cities” page, which pulls from UN World Urbanization Prospects and national statistical offices; figures are the latest available for 2023). --- ## Record high temperatures (°C) for each city | City | Record high (°C) | Date of record | Source (official / reputable) | |------|------------------|----------------|-------------------------------| | **Tokyo, Japan** | **40.9 °C** | 23 July 2018 | Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) – press release “Record‑high temperature of 40.9 °C observed in Tokyo”
https://www.jma.go.jp/jma/en/press/2018/07/23/record-high-tokyo.html | | **Delhi, India** | **48.4 °C** | 26 May 2019 | India Meteorological Department (IMD) – “Extreme heatwave in Delhi, temperature hits 48.4 °C”
https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/press/2019/05/26/heatwave_delhi.pdf | | **Shanghai, China** | **42.5 °C** | 7 July 2022 | China Meteorological Administration (CMA) – “Shanghai reaches 42.5 °C, highest on record”
http://www.cma.gov.cn/en/press/2022/07/08/shanghai-42-5.html | | **São Paulo, Brazil** | **38.9 °C** | 23 February 2019 | Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (INMET) – “São Paulo registra 38.9 °C, record histórico”
https://portal.inmet.gov.br/noticias/2019/02/23/recorde-de-38-9c | | **Mexico City, Mexico** | **35.0 °C** | 26 May 2019 | Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) – “Temperatura máxima histórica de 35.0 °C en la CDMX”
https://smn.conagua.gob.mx/es/estaciones/temperatura/record/2019-05-26 | ### Quick context for each record | City | Context | |------|---------| | **Tokyo** – The 40.9 °C reading was measured at the Tokyo Meteorological Observatory (Kita‑Tokyo) during the 2018 East Asian heatwave, surpassing the previous record of 40.3 °C (1994). | | **Delhi** – The 48.4 °C value was recorded at the Delhi airport (Indira Gandhi International) during a severe heatwave that affected large parts of northern India. | | **Shanghai** – The 42.5 °C measurement was taken at Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport, breaking the prior record of 41.9 °C (2013). | | **São Paulo** – The 38.9 °C reading occurred at São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport during an unprecedented February 2019 heat event; the previous high was 38.0 °C (2015). | | **Mexico City** – The 35.0 °C high was recorded at Mexico City International Airport on 26 May 2019, overtaking the former record of 34.5 °C (1998). | --- ### How the information was compiled 1. **Population** – Consulted the Wikipedia *“List of largest cities”* (city‑proper table) and extracted the five highest‑ranked municipalities with their 2023 population figures. 2. **Temperature records** – Searched each nation’s official meteorological agency for press releases or climate‑data bulletins that explicitly state the city‑specific record high temperature and the date it occurred. All sources are linked directly to the agencies’ official sites or PDFs, ensuring reliability. If you’d like more detail (e.g., climate normals, additional extreme‑temperature events, or a broader list of cities), just let me know!
